*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health
emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20 (https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of
September 14, 2021, at 1:00 P.M. for closed session as follows:

1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking
Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at
athompson@cityofinglewood.org and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution
to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to
8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject
matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M.
and prior to the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.
Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

2. In Person: The Library Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library) will be open to provide members
of the public with an opportunity to address the Legislative Body on Closed Session Items.

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  September 14, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
September 14, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Jeffery Lewis  Senior Assistant City Attorney
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager/CFO
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item on the Agenda.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking
Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/ Parking
Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a
quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/ Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/ Parking
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Parking Authority/ Joint Powers Authority
officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager/Acting Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking Authority,
and Joint Powers Authority.
   September 14, 2021

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to
  address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Parking Authority/ Joint
  Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas.
  Cynthia Oliver, District 1 resident, spoke concerning the parking permit program.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  August 27, 2021, in the amount of $2,347,186.39, dated September 2, 2021, in the
  amount of $3,922,021.73, dated September 10, 2021, in the amount of $2,195,514.87, are
  hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority
  Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands are so
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman /
  Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council
  Member Faulk that the Minutes for the Council Meeting held on April 27, 2021, and the
  Special Meeting on April 27, 2021, be approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Ronald Banks for alleged property damage; stray baseballs from Darby Park on
  March 20, April 24, May 15, and June 27, 2021.
  2. Kenneth Kelly for alleged vehicle damage; protruding rebar on June 24, 2021.
  3. Linda Price for alleged vehicle damage; fallen tree branch on July 27, 2021.
  4. Itzchel Sabarantnam for alleged personal injury; trip and fall on January 13, 2021.
  B. Reject Insufficient Claim Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Tadele Hadush for alleged personal injury; pavement condition on April 6, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject Claims listed as A-1 through A-4; and 2) Reject
  Insufficient Claim listed as B-1. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AMENDMENT SEVEN TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-201 APPROVED – COUNTY
  OF LOS ANGELES WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AGING AND
  COMMUNITY SERVICES (WDACS); RESOLUTION NO. 21-143 ADOPTED –
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET. Staff report dated
  September 14, 2021, was presented recommending approval of Amendment Seven for
  the Elderly Nutrition Program Services Subaward Number ENP202107 (City Agreement
  No. 20-201) with County of Los Angeles Workforce Development Aging and
  Community Services (WDACS) to reallocate CARES Act funding in the amount of
  $108,542 and allocate CDBG-CV1 grant funding in the amount of $36,000 for provision
  of the Elderly Nutrition Program (ENP).

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment Seven to Agreement No. 20-201;
  and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-143 entitled:

  2
   September 14, 2021

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, AMENDING THE 2020-2021 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  RECEIVE $36,000 FROM THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES
  WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AGING AND COMMUNITY
  SERVICES FOR PROVISION OF THE ELDERLY NUTRITION
  PROGRAM

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  AGREEMENT NO. 21-238 APPROVED – COUNTRY HILLS ANIMAL CLINIC.
  Staff report dated September 14, 2021, was presented recommending approval of the
  attached three (3)-year agreement (with the option to extend one additional year) with
  Country Hills Animal Clinic to provide veterinary services for the Police Department’s
  Canine Unit.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-238 in an annual amount not to
  exceed $20,000 (total of $60,000). The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-078 APPROVED – DR. SUSAN
  SAXE-CLIFFORD. Staff report dated September 14, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 19-078 with Dr. Susan
  Saxe-Clifford, extending the agreement an additional year (with the option to extend the
  term for an additional one (1) year) to continue providing psychological evaluation
  services for the Police Department.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 19-078 in an
  amount not to exceed $30,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 21-239 APPROVED – BEST
  CONTRACTING SERVICES, INC.; RESOLUTION NO. 21-144 ADOPTED –
  AMENDING THE 2020-2021 ANNUAL BUDGET. Staff report dated September 14,
  2021, was presented recommending award of a contract and approval of an agreement
  with Best Contracting Services, Inc., for the Service Center Yard Roofing Project, per
  Bid No. CB-21-01.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 21-239 in
  a total amount not to exceed $1,269,952.31 (includes a ten percent (10%) contingency in
  the amount of $115,450.21); and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-144 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA AMENDING THE CITY’S 2020-2021 ANNUAL
  BUDGET TO FUND THE PUBLIC WORKS SERVICE CENTER
  YARD ROOF PROJECT FY 2020-21

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 21-145 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2020-2021 ANNUAL
  BUDGET FOR THE CITY LAST-MILE TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT
  P658. Staff report dated September 14, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of

  3
   September 14, 2021

  a resolution amending the 2020-2021 Annual Budget to ensure adequate appropriations
  for the City Last-Mile Transit Connector Project P658.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 21-145 entitled:

  A RESOLUTIO

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101&131.8  AGREEMENT NOS. 21-240 APPROVED – ACQUISITION OF THE PROPERTY
  BY THE INGLEWOOD HOUSING AUTHORITY FROM SELLER CAROL
  PARK; AGREEMENT NO. 21-240B APPROVED – ACQUISITION AND
  RESALE OF THE PROPERTY ACCORDING TO RESIDENTAL PURCHASE;
  AGREEMENT NO. 21-241 APPROVED – RESALE OF THE PROPERTY FROM
  THE INGLEWOOD HOUSING AUTHORITY AND HOMEBUYER LOTTERY
  WINNER SHARRELL LITTLE; AGREEMENT NO. 21-241B APPROVED –
  REIMBUSEMENT OF THE GENERAL FUND; CHAIRMAN AUTHORIZED TO
  SIGN DOCUMENTS. Staff report dated September 14, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of the acquisition and resale of the Property located at 730 Cory
  Drive #9, Inglewood, CA 90302.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-240 acquisition of the Property by
  the Inglewood Housing Authority from seller Carol Park for up to $542,000 plus closing
  cost;
  2) Approve Agreement No. 21-240B the resale of the Property from the Inglewood
  Housing Authority to affordable income household buyer and Homebuyer Assistance
  Program lottery winner Sharrell Little at an affordable resale price of $312,500; and 3)
  Authorize the General Fund to pay for the acquisition and resale costs associated thereto.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Housing Authority Chairman Butts, and seconded by Housing Authority
  Member Morales that the Housing Authority does hereby: 1)  Approve the ac
  ording to residential purchase Agreement No. 21-241 and the assignment of Agreement
  No. 21-241B addendum documents hereto attached; 2) Authorize the Chairman to sign
  and deliver all pertinent acquisition and resale documents associated with this property
  transaction, as well as non-substantive escrow documents to acquire and resell the
  Property; and 3) Reimburse the General Fund for any advances necessary to consummate
  the transactions. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  ORDINANCE NO. 21-15 ADOPTED – ESTABLISHING PAY RANGE
  ASSIGNMENT AND CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2021-2022. Staff report dated September 14, 2021, was presented recommending
  adoption of Ordinance No. 21-15, establishing pay range assignment and conditions of
  employment for Fiscal Year 2021-2022.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that Ordinance No. 21-15 entitled:

  4
 September 14, 2021

  which was introduced at the meeting held on August 24, 2021, be adopted. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  CLOSED SESSION – PENDING LITIGATION - YOLANDA TOBIN V. CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD. Closed Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; City
  Council Conference with Legal Counsel regarding Pending Litigation Pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Yolanda Tobin v. City of Inglewood, et al;
  LASC Case No. 19STCV08190.

  Status Given; No Action Taken.

  REPORTS - CITY CLERK. City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, reminded residents about
  Election Day and advised them to exercise their rights to vote. She also shared
  information about drop box locations, polling locations, and hours of operation. She
  mentioned the NFL Headquarters Groundbreaking Event she attended and thanked Mrs.
  Sharon Mackey & the Circle of Women for honoring her as a Woman of Excellence.
  Additionally, she congratulated Thomas Bunn and the Media Team for winning the
  Savvy Award for the Best Public Service Announcement in the Country. Finally, she
  reminded the residents about National Hispanic Heritage Month beginning September 15,
  2021.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Pablo Olemon, District 4 resident, stated that he favored the parking permit program but
  inquired if the program could be implemented, such as the City of Lennox. He also
  suggested widening the streets in certain areas of District 4.

  Melissa Barlow, District 1 resident, commented that she signed a petition back in 2009
  requesting speed bumps being placed on her street. She stated that many accidents have
  occurred on her street and asked for immediate attention to this matter.

  Cedric Mc Claghlie commented that the bike lanes on Hillcrest are not clean, which
  makes it difficult for him to ride his bike.

  Council Member Dotson left the dais at 2:50 p.m.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts adjourned the meeting in
